scenarios.name: heating_season_high_load
scenarios.description: A January afternoon: the loop is drawing everything the plant can make, pumps at 70% and supply water at 71 degC. Full-temperature water at full flow is the plant doing its job.

scenarios.name: mild_day_supply_temperature_reset_down
scenarios.description: The healthy version of the fault's own weather: pumps loafing at 22% because the building barely needs heat, and a working reset has taken the supply water down to 49 degC to match. Low load is not the finding; low load with hot water is.

scenarios.name: low_load_with_full_temperature_water
scenarios.description: The fault as PNNL-27338 4.4.2 states it: pumps at 20% and supply water at 60 degC, held for the full alarm_delay. The boiler is making design-day water for a loop that is barely drawing, and the alarm asserts at t = 3600 s.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_exactly_at_the_low_load_threshold
scenarios.description: Speed boundary, on the line: 35.0% with 60 degC water. `Reals.LessThreshold` is strict, so 35.0 is not below 35.0 and the loop does not count as lightly loaded.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_one_tenth_below_the_low_load_threshold
scenarios.description: Speed boundary, from below: 34.9% is lightly loaded, so the same 60 degC supply water alarms at 3600 s.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_one_tenth_above_the_low_load_threshold
scenarios.description: Speed boundary, from above: 35.1% and nothing is reported. With the on-the-line case, this pins the threshold from all three sides.

scenarios.name: hws_temp_exactly_at_the_high_supply_threshold
scenarios.description: Temperature boundary, on the line: supply water at exactly 54.4 degC with the pumps at 20%. `Reals.GreaterThreshold` is strict, so the plant reads clear. Both the vector and the parameter spell 54.4, so the two are the same double and the comparison is decided by strictness rather than by rounding.

scenarios.name: hws_temp_one_tenth_above_the_high_supply_threshold
scenarios.description: Temperature boundary, from above: a tenth of a degree warmer at 54.5 degC, same light load, and the alarm arrives at 3600 s.

scenarios.name: hws_temp_one_tenth_below_the_high_supply_threshold
scenarios.description: Temperature boundary, from below: 54.3 degC reads clear, which with the two vectors above pins this threshold from all three sides.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_exactly_at_the_evaluability_floor
scenarios.description: Evaluability boundary, on the line: 10.0% is not above 10.0%, so the loop is not judged to be circulating. yLoopOk is false for the whole run and the 60 degC supply water is never assessed.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_one_tenth_below_the_evaluability_floor
scenarios.description: Evaluability boundary, from below: 9.9% with hot water. Same verdict and same reason — a drive at its lowest command is not evidence that the loop is moving water past the coils.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_one_tenth_above_the_evaluability_floor
scenarios.description: Evaluability boundary, from above: 10.1% is circulating, so the same hot water is now a finding and alarms at 3600 s. The floor is pinned from all three sides.

scenarios.name: pump_off_with_hot_standing_water
scenarios.description: The false positive the evaluability floor exists to prevent: an overnight setback with the pumps stopped and 65 degC water still standing in the boiler. Speed reads 0%, which is below 35% and would otherwise satisfy the reference's two-condition test for as long as the water stays hot. yLoopOk is false, so the host reads NO_EVAL rather than a fault.

scenarios.name: supply_temperature_climbs_mid_run
scenarios.description: A reset schedule losing its way: the loop sits at 20% all morning with 50 degC water, and at t = 1800 s the supply temperature climbs to 60 degC. The clock starts at the crossing, not at the start of the run, so the alarm lands at 5400 s.

scenarios.name: pump_speed_rises_and_restarts_the_clock
scenarios.description: Persistence is continuous, not accumulated. A morning pickup takes the pumps to 40% for 600 s at t = 1800 s and the elapsed time is discarded rather than paused: the alarm lands at 6000 s, one full alarm_delay after the loop settles back to 20%.

scenarios.name: condition_ends_on_the_maturity_tick
scenarios.description: Delay edge from below: the condition holds from t = 0 and the supply temperature drops to 50 degC at exactly 3600 s, the tick the timer matures on. The input is false when the timer comes due, so a full hour of overheated water is never reported.

scenarios.name: condition_ends_one_tick_later
scenarios.description: Delay edge from above: the same run held 300 s longer asserts at exactly 3600 s and clears at 3900 s. With the vector above, both sides of the delay edge are pinned.

scenarios.name: supply_temperature_resets_down_after_the_alarm
scenarios.description: Recovery, and the operator's confirmation that a reset schedule took: the supply setpoint comes down and the water follows to 48 degC at t = 5400 s. yFault falls on that tick with no release delay, and yLoopOk stays true throughout — the loop was circulating the whole time, so the clearing verdict is a real one.

scenarios.name: pump_stops_after_the_alarm
scenarios.description: The other way yFault falls, and the reason yLoopOk is a boundary output: the water stays at 60 degC but the pumps stop at t = 5400 s. yFault clears exactly as it does when the temperature resets down, and only yLoopOk says which of the two happened — here, nothing was fixed and the loop simply stopped being evaluable.
